candidates: In `build-dev.ts`, `presets.apply('core', {})` is called once early and then again after `loadAllPresets` rebuilds the full preset chain. Any config values (such as `allowedHosts`) that are used for security checks, `logger.warn` messages, or startup output must be read from the second (final) preset call—not captured in the first pass—so the values reflect the complete, merged configuration and do not produce stale or misleading results.

Host/origin validation middleware must not contain an implicit allow-all bypass based on the server's bind address (e.g., `host === '0.0.0.0'`) combined with an empty allowlist. Validation should always run by default; if the operator genuinely wants to permit all hosts they must explicitly configure `allowedHosts: true`. Implicit bypasses defeat the purpose of the security feature.

JSDoc and inline comments on request-validation utilities must accurately describe HTTP/1.1 header semantics. Modern browsers always include a `Host` header for every HTTP/1.1+ request regardless of how the navigation originated (address bar, same-origin fetch, etc.); do not claim that normal browser requests lack a `Host` header, as this misleads future maintainers about when the validation actually fires.

Test fixture objects shared across multiple test cases should be typed with the actual interface or `ConstructorParameters<typeof T>[N]` rather than cast with `as any`. Using `as any` silently hides shape regressions when a constructor's parameter type evolves, removing the type-safety benefit that would otherwise catch test breakage at compile time.
